mainTopic: The sources for the eating and benefit prohibitions of בשר בחלב, and the rules for refuting a קל וחומר and a במה הצד.
overview: This amud asks where we learn that בשר בחלב is forbidden to eat and forbidden for הנאה. רבי יוחנן challenges ריש לקיש: רבי already learned the eating ban from the extra ״לא תאכלנו״. ריש לקיש answers that his own source adds the ban on benefit, and the גמרא shows that רבי learns benefit from a גזירה שוה of קדוש and קדש. Then come more sources: דבי רבי אליעזר learns it from selling a נבלה, and דבי רבי ישמעאל learns it from the three times the תורה writes ״לא תבשל גדי״. איסי בן יהודה learns eating from טרפה and benefit from a קל וחומר from ערלה, which the גמרא defends using חמץ and כלאי הכרם. The גמרא then asks why איסי needs a גזירה שוה at all, and why it needed כלאי הכרם instead of a במה הצד. This leads רב אשי and רב מרדכי into a back-and-forth about how each kind of proof may be refuted. The amud ends as רב מרדכי begins a new version of ריש לקיש's teaching, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Why invent a new source when רבי already taught one?
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן challenges ריש לקיש: רבי already taught that the second ״לא תאכלנו״ is about בשר בחלב, so why bring a new derivation?
steps.simpleTranslation: Is what רבי taught so 'ugly' that you need a new source? רבי taught: 'You shall not eat it' is talking about meat in milk.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן attacks ריש לקיש's new source by pointing to an older, well-known source from רבי. He is basically saying: 'What's wrong with רבי's source?'
steps.deeperAnalysis: ריש לקיש just derived the איסור of eating בשר בחלב from the קרבן פסח. רבי יוחנן points out that רבי already found a פסוק for this: the extra ״לא תאכלנו״ in דברים 12:25. If an accepted source already exists, the new one seems unnecessary.

keyTerms.meaning: Ugly, meaning not good enough. Used here as a sharp way of asking 'what's wrong with it?'
Taught (a ברייתא or teaching)
Meat cooked with milk
The פסוק is talking about

steps.confusionAlert: This line opens in the middle of a conversation. The speaker is רבי יוחנן, talking to ריש לקיש right after ריש לקיש brought his source from the קרבן פסח.

phrases.english: Is this that רבי taught ugly?
phrases.notes: רבי יוחנן is speaking to ריש לקיש. He means: what's wrong with רבי's source that you need a new one?

phrases.english: "You shall not eat it"
phrases.notes: דברים 12:25. This is the second time the פסוק says it, right after the one about blood.

phrases.english: the verse is speaking about meat in milk.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges ריש לקיש's derivation from the קרבן פסח, which came just before this section.
steps.kashyaTarget: ריש לקיש's new source for the איסור of eating בשר בחלב
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: An established source from רבי already exists, so a new derivation seems unnecessary.

steps.title: How רבי knows the פסוק is about meat and milk
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא of רבי continues. It explains why ״לא תאכלנו״ refers to בשר בחלב and not some other איסור, using the rule of דבר הלמד מעניינו.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might ask: is the פסוק really about meat in milk, or about any other איסור in the תורה? Go learn from the thirteen rules for explaining the תורה. One of them is: a matter is learned from its context. What are the nearby פסוקים talking about? Something made of two types. So here too, it is about two types.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא continues quoting רבי's teaching to show it is solid. It proves that the extra ״לא תאכלנו״ is about mixing two kinds, meaning meat and milk.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question is why this extra ״לא תאכלנו״ should point to בשר בחלב rather than any other forbidden food. The answer uses דבר הלמד מעניינו: the surrounding פסוקים deal with something that has two natures (redeemed קדשים, which may be eaten like חולין but may not be sheared or worked like קדשים). So this איסור must also involve two kinds, and בשר בחלב is exactly that.

keyTerms.meaning: The thirteen rules for explaining the תורה (of רבי ישמעאל)
Is explained or expounded
A matter learned from its context, meaning from the surrounding פסוקים
Two kinds, something combining two types

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that רבי's source for the איסור of eating בשר בחלב is strong, which makes רבי יוחנן's challenge sharper: why would ריש לקיש need anything else?

phrases.aramaic: אַתָּה אוֹמֵר בְּבָשָׂר בְּחָלָב הַכָּתוּב מְדַבֵּר,
phrases.english: Do you say the verse is speaking about meat in milk,

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ אֵינוֹ אֶלָּא בְּאֶחָד מִכׇּל הָאִיסּוּרִין שֶׁבַּתּוֹרָה?
phrases.english: or is it only about one of all the prohibitions in the Torah?
You say: go out and learn

phrases.aramaic: מִשְּׁלֹשׁ עֶשְׂרֵה מִדּוֹת שֶׁהַתּוֹרָה נִדְרֶשֶׁת בָּהֶן,
phrases.english: from the thirteen principles by which the Torah is expounded,
a matter that is learned from its context.
What is the passage speaking about? About two types,
phrases.notes: The nearby פסוקים talk about redeemed קדשים, which are partly like חולין and partly like holy animals.

phrases.english: so too here, about two types.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַתָּה אוֹמֵר בְּבָשָׂר בְּחָלָב הַכָּתוּב מְדַבֵּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes quoting רבי's teaching, which רבי יוחנן used in his challenge.
steps.raayaObject: That ״לא תאכלנו״ (דברים 12:25) refers to בשר בחלב
steps.raayaSupportSource: The rule of דבר הלמד מעניינו: the context deals with 'two types', and so does this איסור

steps.title: רבי's source covers eating, but not benefit
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש answers: from רבי's פסוק alone we would only know that eating בשר בחלב is forbidden, not benefiting from it. His source from the קרבן פסח teaches the הנאה prohibition too.
steps.simpleTranslation: If we only had that source, I would have said this applies only to eating, but benefit is allowed. So my source teaches us otherwise.
steps.whatsHappening: ריש לקיש defends his new source by showing it teaches something רבי's source does not: that you may not even benefit from בשר בחלב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי's פסוק says ״לא תאכלנו״, which speaks only about eating. ריש לקיש's source compares בשר בחלב to a disqualified קרבן פסח, which is forbidden even for benefit. So his source is still needed, because it adds the איסור הנאה.

keyTerms.meaning: I would have thought (the mistaken first assumption)
These words apply only to... (limits the rule)
Eating
Benefit, using something for any gain
It teaches us (otherwise)

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the basis for the הלכה that בשר בחלב is אסור בהנאה: you may not sell it or use it in any way, not only eat it.

phrases.english: If from that one alone,
phrases.notes: ריש לקיש is answering now. 'That one' means רבי's פסוק, ״לא תאכלנו״.

phrases.english: I would have said: this applies only to eating,
but to benefit, not;
so it teaches us otherwise.
phrases.notes: 'It' is ריש לקיש's own source from the קרבן פסח.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבי יוחנן's challenge from step 1.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Shows the new source teaches an additional law (הנאה) not covered by the existing source
steps.terutzHavaAmina: With only רבי's source, בשר בחלב would be forbidden to eat but permitted for benefit.
steps.terutzMaskana: ריש לקיש's source is needed to forbid הנאה as well.

steps.title: Where does רבי learn the benefit prohibition?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: if רבי's פסוק only covers eating, where does רבי get the איסור הנאה of בשר בחלב?
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי, where does he learn that benefit is forbidden?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a follow-up question that sets up the next step: רבי must also hold that בשר בחלב is forbidden for benefit, so what is his source?
steps.deeperAnalysis: ריש לקיש just said רבי's פסוק teaches only eating. Since רבי surely agrees that הנאה is forbidden too, he must have some other source, and the גמרא wants to find it.

keyTerms.meaning: From where does he know it?

phrases.english: And רבי, from where does he know benefit is forbidden?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follows from ריש לקיש's answer that רבי's source covers only eating.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: רבי's source for the איסור הנאה of בשר בחלב

steps.title: רבי learns it from the words קדוש and קדש
steps.stepSummary: רבי learns הנאה through a גזירה שוה: ״כי עם קדוש אתה״ near בשר בחלב is compared to ״ולא יהיה קדש בבני ישראל״, which is an איסור of pleasure, so בשר בחלב is forbidden for benefit too.
steps.simpleTranslation: He learns it from here: it says here 'For you are a holy (קדוש) people to ה׳', and it says elsewhere 'There shall not be a קדש among the children of Israel'. Just as there it is about benefit, so too here it is about benefit.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question by giving רבי's source: a word comparison that turns בשר בחלב into an איסור הנאה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק of בשר בחלב (דברים 14:21) contains the words ״כי עם קדוש אתה״ right before ״לא תבשל גדי״. The פסוק forbidding a קדש (דברים 23:18) uses the same root. The קדש איסור is about pleasure and benefit, not eating, so through this link בשר בחלב also becomes forbidden for הנאה.

keyTerms.meaning: He derives it
Holy, said of the Jewish people
A person involved in forbidden relations (same root as קדוש)
Just as there, so too here. The language of a גזירה שוה.
A comparison based on similar words in two פסוקים

steps.whatToRemember: Both רבי and ריש לקיש agree that בשר בחלב is forbidden to eat and forbidden for benefit. They only disagree about the sources: ריש לקיש uses the קרבן פסח, and רבי uses ״לא תאכלנו״ for eating and the קדוש/קדש comparison for benefit.

phrases.english: He derives it from here:

phrases.aramaic: נֶאֱמַר כָּאן ״כִּי עַם קָדוֹשׁ אַתָּה לַה׳״,
phrases.english: it is said here: "For you are a holy people to ה׳",
phrases.notes: דברים 14:21. The same פסוק ends with 'Do not cook a kid in its mother's milk.'

phrases.english: and it is said further on
"There shall not be a קדש among the children of Israel",
phrases.notes: דברים 23:18

phrases.english: just as there it is about benefit,
phrases.notes: The איסור of a קדש is about pleasure, not eating.

phrases.english: so too here it is about benefit.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 4.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי derives the איסור הנאה through a גזירה שוה of קדוש (דברים 14:21) and קדש (דברים 23:18).

steps.title: The school of רבי אליעזר: you may sell a נבלה, but not after cooking it in milk
steps.stepSummary: דבי רבי אליעזר learns the איסור הנאה of בשר בחלב from the פסוק that lets you sell a נבלה to a נכרי and then right away says not to cook a kid in milk.
steps.simpleTranslation: The school of רבי אליעזר taught: the פסוק says, ״Do not eat any נבלה... you may sell it to a foreigner... do not cook a kid in its mother's milk.״ The תורה is saying: when you sell it, do not cook it in milk and then sell it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another source for the איסור הנאה of בשר בחלב, from the school of רבי אליעזר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the same פסוק, the תורה allows selling a נבלה to a נכרי and then right after forbids cooking meat in milk. Putting them side by side teaches that selling is allowed, but not once the meat was cooked in milk. Selling is a kind of benefit, so this shows בשר בחלב is אסור בהנאה.

keyTerms.meaning: An animal that died without proper שחיטה
The school of (the students of a certain sage)
You sell it
You cook it (in milk)

phrases.english: The school of Rabbi Eliezer taught:
"You shall not eat any carcass [etc.]"
phrases.notes: דברים 14:21. וגו׳ means "and the rest of the פסוק," which allows selling it to a foreigner and ends with not cooking a kid in milk.

phrases.english: The Torah said: when you sell it,
do not cook it in milk and then sell it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a different source for the איסור הנאה that רבי learned through a גזירה שוה in Step 5.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Because the פסוק lets you sell a נבלה and then forbids בשר בחלב, it teaches that meat cooked in milk may not be sold, so it is אסור בהנאה.

steps.title: The school of רבי ישמעאל: three פסוקים for three prohibitions
steps.stepSummary: דבי רבי ישמעאל teaches that the Torah repeats ״לא תבשל גדי בחלב אמו״ three times to give three separate prohibitions: eating, benefit, and cooking.
steps.simpleTranslation: The school of רבי ישמעאל taught: ״Do not cook a kid in its mother's milk״ is written three times. One is for the prohibition of eating, one for the prohibition of benefit, and one for the prohibition of cooking.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a third approach: the תורה wrote the same פסוק three times, and each one teaches a different prohibition.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תורה does not repeat words for nothing, so each of the three times ״לא תבשל״ appears is used for its own law. This way one source covers all three issues at once: eating, benefit, and the act of cooking itself.

keyTerms.meaning: Three times
Prohibition of eating
Prohibition of having any benefit
Prohibition of cooking

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the best-known source for the rule that בשר בחלב has three separate prohibitions: cooking, eating, and benefit.

phrases.english: The school of Rabbi Yishmael taught:

phrases.aramaic: ״לֹא תְבַשֵּׁל גְּדִי בַּחֲלֵב אִמּוֹ״ שָׁלֹשׁ פְּעָמִים,
phrases.english: "You shall not cook a kid in its mother's milk" is written three times,
phrases.notes: שמות 23:19, שמות 34:26, דברים 14:21.

phrases.english: one for the prohibition of eating,
and one for the prohibition of benefit,
and one for the prohibition of cooking.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Another alternative source, this time covering eating, benefit, and cooking all from the repeated פסוק.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The three times the Torah writes ״לא תבשל״ teach three prohibitions: eating, benefit, and cooking.

steps.title: איסי בן יהודה: eating בשר בחלב is forbidden, learned from טרפה
steps.stepSummary: איסי בן יהודה learns the eating prohibition of בשר בחלב through a גזירה שוה: the word קדוש near בשר בחלב is compared to קדש near the prohibition of eating טרפה.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא teaches: איסי בן יהודה says, from where do we know בשר בחלב is forbidden? Here it says ״For you are a holy people,״ and elsewhere it says ״You shall be holy people to Me, and do not eat meat torn in the field.״ Just as there it is forbidden to eat, here too it is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא with איסי בן יהודה's own source, starting with the prohibition of eating בשר בחלב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word ״קדוש״ appears next to בשר בחלב, and ״קדש״ appears next to טרפה, which the תורה clearly forbids eating. This shared word links the two, so בשר בחלב is also forbidden to eat. This step only covers eating; the next step asks about benefit.

keyTerms.meaning: A holy people
An animal torn or fatally injured, forbidden to eat
Here... there (the two פסוקים being compared)
Just as... so too (the formula of comparison)

phrases.english: It is taught in a baraita: Isi ben Yehuda says:
From where do we know that meat in milk is forbidden?
phrases.notes: He means forbidden to eat; benefit comes next.

phrases.english: It says here: "For you are a holy people,"
phrases.notes: דברים 14:21.

phrases.english: and it says there: "You shall be holy people to Me,
phrases.notes: שמות 22:30.

phrases.english: and meat torn in the field you shall not eat."
Just as there it is forbidden,
so too here it is forbidden.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A fourth approach; uses the same ״כי עם קדוש אתה״ that רבי used in Step 5, but links it to טרפה for eating instead of to הנאה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Through a גזירה שוה of קדוש/קדש with טרפה, eating בשר בחלב is forbidden.

steps.title: איסי בן יהודה asks: where do we learn the benefit prohibition?
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא notes that the comparison to טרפה only proves an eating prohibition, and asks where the prohibition of benefit comes from.
steps.simpleTranslation: But this only teaches eating. From where do we learn benefit?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא is setting up the next move: it admits its proof only covers eating, and asks for a source for benefit.
steps.deeperAnalysis: טרפה is a prohibition of eating, so the comparison only carries over eating. A separate source is needed to forbid using or selling בשר בחלב.

keyTerms.meaning: I only have (proof for)...
From where (do we learn)?

phrases.english: I only have proof for eating;
from where do we know benefit is forbidden?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאֵין לִי אֶלָּא בַּאֲכִילָה, בַּהֲנָאָה מִנַּיִן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Points out the limit of Step 8's proof: it only covers eating.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A source that בשר בחלב is also אסור בהנאה.

steps.title: A קל וחומר from ערלה proves benefit is forbidden
steps.stepSummary: איסי בן יהודה answers with a קל וחומר: ערלה, where no sin was done, is forbidden for benefit, so בשר בחלב, where a sin was done in cooking it, should surely be forbidden for benefit.
steps.simpleTranslation: You can say a קל וחומר: ערלה, where no sin was done with it, is still forbidden for benefit. בשר בחלב, where a sin was done with it, should surely be forbidden for benefit!
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers its own question using a קל וחומר from ערלה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Growing fruit in a tree's first three years is not a sin at all, yet the fruit (ערלה) is forbidden for benefit. Cooking meat in milk is itself a sin, so this mixture is more serious. If the lighter case is forbidden for benefit, the more serious case must be too.

keyTerms.meaning: A logical proof from a lighter case to a stricter case
Fruit from a tree's first three years, forbidden for benefit
A sin was done with it
Is it not logical?

steps.whatToRemember: The גמרא has now shown several ways to learn the איסור הנאה of בשר בחלב: ריש לקיש from פסח, רבי from a גזירה שוה, דבי רבי אליעזר from selling a נבלה, דבי רבי ישמעאל from the three פסוקים, and איסי בן יהודה from a קל וחומר from ערלה.
steps.confusionAlert: The "sin" in בשר בחלב is the act of cooking meat with milk, which is itself forbidden. With ערלה, planting and growing the fruit is no sin at all.

phrases.english: You can say a kal vachomer:

phrases.aramaic: וּמָה עׇרְלָה שֶׁלֹּא נֶעֶבְדָה בָּהּ עֲבֵירָה –
phrases.english: If orla, with which no sin was done,
is forbidden for benefit,
then meat in milk, with which a sin was done,
is it not logical that it is forbidden for benefit!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Directly answers the question of Step 9.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A קל וחומר from ערלה: if ערלה, with no sin, is אסור בהנאה, then בשר בחלב, made through a sin, is surely אסור בהנאה.

steps.title: ערלה is special: it was never permitted
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes back on the קל וחומר: ערלה was forbidden from the start, but meat and milk were each permitted before being cooked together.
steps.simpleTranslation: But ערלה is special, because it never had a time when it was permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the קל וחומר from step 10 by finding a stricter feature in ערלה that בשר בחלב does not have.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A קל וחומר only works if the source case is truly the weaker one. ערלה fruit is forbidden from the moment it grows, while meat and milk were both fine before cooking. Maybe that is why ערלה is forbidden for benefit, so we cannot carry it over to בשר בחלב.

keyTerms.meaning: "What about...?" A standard way to show that the source case has a special strict feature, which breaks the קל וחומר
A time when the item was fit and permitted
Fruit from a tree's first three years, forbidden to eat and to benefit from

steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא is not saying the קל וחומר is wrong in its conclusion. It is only saying that ערלה by itself is not a strong enough source.

phrases.english: What is special about orla?

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁכֵּן לֹא הָיְתָה לָהּ שְׁעַת הַכּוֹשֶׁר.
phrases.english: That it never had a time when it was fit.

steps.triggerLanguage: מָה לְעׇרְלָה, שֶׁכֵּן לֹא הָיְתָה לָהּ שְׁעַת הַכּוֹשֶׁר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Refutes the קל וחומר of step 10 by pointing to a stricter feature of ערלה
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The קל וחומר from ערלה alone
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: ערלה never had a permitted moment, so it may be stricter than בשר בחלב

steps.title: חמץ בפסח shows that an item once permitted can still be forbidden for benefit
steps.stepSummary: חמץ was permitted before פסח, yet on פסח it is forbidden for benefit. So the 'never permitted' feature is not what causes a benefit prohibition.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let חמץ on פסח prove the point: it had a time when it was permitted, and still it is forbidden for benefit.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the objection by bringing a different case, חמץ בפסח, which does not have ערלה's special feature but is still forbidden for benefit.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The objection said benefit prohibitions might depend on never having been permitted. חמץ was fine before פסח, yet it is still forbidden for benefit. So that feature is not required, and the reasoning can reach בשר בחלב.

keyTerms.meaning: "Will prove." Brings a second case to cancel the special feature found in the first case
Leavened food on פסח
Forbidden to get any benefit from

phrases.english: Leavened bread on Passover will prove it,
since it had a time when it was fit,
and yet it is forbidden for benefit.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the refutation of step 11 by bringing a case without ערלה's special feature
steps.raayaObject: That an item which was once permitted can still be forbidden for benefit

steps.title: חמץ is special: it carries כרת
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes back again: חמץ is punished with כרת, which בשר בחלב is not, so חמץ may be stricter.
steps.simpleTranslation: But חמץ on פסח is special, because eating it is punished with כרת.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finds a strict feature in חמץ too, so חמץ alone cannot prove the point either.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Eating חמץ on פסח is punished with כרת, while eating בשר בחלב is not. Maybe the benefit prohibition comes from that severity. So the proof from חמץ does not carry over yet.

keyTerms.meaning: Being "cut off", a severe punishment from Heaven
Punishable

phrases.english: What is special about leavened bread on Passover?
That it is punishable by karet.

steps.triggerLanguage: מָה לְחָמֵץ בַּפֶּסַח, שֶׁכֵּן עָנוּשׁ כָּרֵת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Refutes the proof from חמץ in step 12 by pointing to its כרת penalty
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: חמץ carries כרת, so it is stricter than בשר בחלב

steps.title: כלאי הכרם has no כרת but is still forbidden for benefit
steps.stepSummary: כלאי הכרם is not punished with כרת, yet it is forbidden for benefit. This removes the last objection.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let כלאי הכרם prove the point: it is not punished with כרת, and still it is forbidden for benefit.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a third case without חמץ's special feature, which supports the benefit prohibition for בשר בחלב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The worry was that only very severe items, with כרת, are forbidden for benefit. כלאי הכרם has no כרת and is still forbidden for benefit, so that feature is not required. Now the reasoning for בשר בחלב stands.

keyTerms.meaning: Grain or vegetables planted together with grapevines in a vineyard, forbidden to eat and to benefit from

steps.whatToRemember: Each source case had a weak point (ערלה: never permitted; חמץ: כרת), but another case without that weak point was always found. So the benefit prohibition of בשר בחלב stands.

phrases.english: Diverse kinds in a vineyard will prove it,
since it is not punishable by karet,
and yet it is forbidden for benefit.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the refutation of step 13 by bringing a case without כרת
steps.raayaObject: That an item without a כרת penalty can still be forbidden for benefit

steps.title: Why not learn the eating prohibition from ערלה too?
steps.stepSummary: If a קל וחומר from ערלה works, it should prove both the eating and the benefit prohibitions, so why does איסי need a גזירה שוה for eating?
steps.simpleTranslation: Why do we need the גזירה שוה? Let us learn everything with a קל וחומר from ערלה: ערלה, where no sin was done, is forbidden both to eat and to benefit from. So בשר בחלב, where a sin was done, should surely be forbidden both to eat and to benefit from!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new challenge to איסי בן יהודה's method. The answer will come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: איסי used a גזירה שוה (step 8) for eating and a קל וחומר (step 10) for benefit. But ערלה is forbidden for both, so the same קל וחומר should give both prohibitions. That makes the גזירה שוה look unnecessary.

keyTerms.meaning: Learning one law from another because the Torah uses the same word in both places
Reasoning that if a lighter case has a rule, a stricter case surely has it
"Let him bring." Let us derive it
"Is it not logical?" The closing line of a קל וחומר

phrases.english: Why do I need the verbal analogy?
phrases.notes: This is the קדוש and קדש comparison from step 8, used for the eating prohibition.

phrases.english: Let all of it be derived by an a fortiori from orla:

phrases.aramaic: וּמָה עׇרְלָה, שֶׁלֹּא נֶעֶבְדָה בָּהּ עֲבֵירָה,
phrases.english: Just as orla, with which no sin was committed,
is forbidden both for eating and for benefit;
meat in milk, with which a sin was committed,

phrases.aramaic: אֵינוֹ דִּין שֶׁאָסוּר בֵּין בַּאֲכִילָה בֵּין בַּהֲנָאָה!
phrases.english: is it not logical that it is forbidden both for eating and for benefit!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the benefit prohibition is secured, the גמרא questions why the separate גזירה שוה for eating is needed
steps.kashyaTarget: איסי בן יהודה's use of a גזירה שוה for the eating prohibition
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The same קל וחומר from ערלה would prove both eating and benefit, so the גזירה שוה seems unnecessary

steps.title: A logical argument for eating could be broken, so a verse-based link is needed
steps.stepSummary: The קל וחומר for eating can be refuted by plowing with an ox and donkey, and by muzzling a cow. In both cases a sin was committed, yet the results are permitted. So איסי needs a גזירה שוה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because one could say: someone who plows with an ox and a donkey together, or who muzzles a cow and threshes with it, proves the point wrong. A sin was committed through them, and yet they are permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from step 15. A קל וחומר for eating would not hold up, so איסי had to use a גזירה שוה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The קל וחומר for eating rests on 'a sin was done in making it' (the cooking), but plowing with mixed animals and muzzling a threshing cow are also sins, and the grain they produce is permitted even to eat. So that reason cannot create an eating prohibition by itself, and איסי needs a גזירה שוה for eating. The benefit קל וחומר in step 10 still stands, because once the גזירה שוה forbids eating בשר בחלב, it is unlike that permitted grain.

keyTerms.meaning: Plowing with an ox and a donkey yoked together, which is forbidden
Muzzling a cow so it cannot eat while it works
Will prove (here: proves the argument wrong)
A sin was committed through them

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that a קל וחומר is only as strong as its logic. A גזירה שוה comes from the wording of the verses, so it cannot be broken by a counter-example like this.

phrases.english: Because one could say:
One who plows with an ox and with a donkey,
phrases.notes: דברים 22:10

phrases.aramaic: וְחוֹסֵם פִּי פָרָה וְדָשׁ בָּהּ יוֹכִיחַ,
phrases.english: and one who muzzles a cow's mouth and threshes with it, will prove it,
phrases.notes: דברים 25:4

phrases.english: for a sin was committed through them, and yet they are permitted.
phrases.notes: He means the grain that comes from this plowing or threshing is still allowed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 15 about why a גזירה שוה is needed for eating.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Shows that the alternative proof (the קל וחומר) can be refuted
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A קל וחומר from ערלה should be enough to forbid eating בשר בחלב.
steps.terutzMaskana: That קל וחומר is refuted by plowing with mixed animals and by muzzling, so a גזירה שוה is needed.

steps.title: Why not combine ערלה and חמץ instead of using כלאי הכרם?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the earlier proof needed כלאי הכרם. It could have let ערלה and חמץ answer each other's weaknesses and then derived the law from what they share, using a במה הצד.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why do I need to say 'כלאי הכרם proves it'? Let us say 'ערלה proves it', let the argument go back around, and let the law come from what the two cases have in common.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why step 14 needed כלאי הכרם at all. It suggests that ערלה and חמץ could cover for each other.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ערלה was pushed aside because it was never permitted. חמץ was pushed aside because it carries כרת. But each one lacks the other's special strictness. So together they show that what makes something forbidden for benefit is the fact that it is forbidden to eat. That shared feature would also apply to בשר בחלב.

keyTerms.meaning: A proof built from the shared feature of two sources
Let the argument go back around to its starting point
Mixed plantings in a vineyard, which are forbidden for benefit

steps.confusionAlert: This is not an attack on the conclusion that בשר בחלב is forbidden for benefit. The question is only why the proof took the route through כלאי הכרם.

phrases.english: Why do I need to say
'diverse kinds in a vineyard prove it'?
phrases.notes: This points back to step 14.

phrases.english: Let us say 'ערלה proves it',
phrases.notes: ערלה answers חמץ's weakness: ערלה has no כרת, and yet it is forbidden for benefit.

phrases.english: and let the argument go back around,
and let it be derived through the common element.

steps.triggerLanguage: לְמָה לִי לְמֵימַר כִּלְאֵי הַכֶּרֶם יוֹכִיחוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the proof chain in steps 11–14 and asks why the כלאי הכרם step was needed.
steps.kashyaTarget: The use of כלאי הכרם in step 14
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: ערלה and חמץ each cancel the other's special strictness, so a במה הצד from the two of them should be enough without כלאי הכרם.

steps.title: רב אשי: נבלה would break the combined proof
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי answers that a במה הצד from ערלה and חמץ fails. נבלה is forbidden to eat, yet it is permitted for benefit.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: Because one could say נבלה proves it wrong, since it is forbidden to eat but permitted for benefit.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי explains why the במה הצד would not work, which is why כלאי הכרם was needed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The shared feature of ערלה and חמץ is 'forbidden to eat'. But נבלה is also forbidden to eat, and it is still permitted for benefit. So being forbidden to eat does not by itself lead to a benefit prohibition, and the במה הצד breaks down.

keyTerms.meaning: An animal that died without proper שחיטה
Forbidden to eat
Permitted for benefit

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said:
Because one could say,
an animal carcass proves it wrong,
for it is forbidden to eat
and yet permitted for benefit.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב אָשֵׁי מִשּׁוּם דְּאִיכָּא לְמֵימַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 17.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Brings a counter-example that breaks the suggested במה הצד
steps.terutzHavaAmina: ערלה and חמץ together could prove the benefit prohibition.
steps.terutzMaskana: נבלה shows that being forbidden to eat does not lead to a benefit prohibition, so כלאי הכרם is needed.

steps.title: רב מרדכי: a במה הצד cannot be broken by an outside case
steps.stepSummary: רב מרדכי quotes ריש לקיש: a במה הצד can only be refuted by a weakness inside its own sources, not by an outside case like נבלה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב מרדכי said to רב אשי: This is what we say in the name of ריש לקיש: any 'common element' proof is refuted from within itself; we do not refute it from the outside world.
steps.whatsHappening: רב מרדכי rejects רב אשי's answer. Bringing in נבלה is not a valid way to break a במה הצד.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to ריש לקיש, you can only knock down a במה הצד by finding a strictness that both of its sources share and the new case lacks. נבלה is an outside case, so it does not count. That means the question of why כלאי הכרם was needed comes back.

keyTerms.meaning: We refute it from within the sources themselves
We do not refute it from an outside case
A refutation of a proof

steps.whatToRemember: ריש לקיש's rule: a במה הצד can only be broken by a shared feature of its own sources, never by an unrelated outside case.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is a general rule about how a במה הצד works, and it applies far beyond this סוגיא.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב מָרְדֳּכַי לְרַב אָשֵׁי:
phrases.english: Rav Mordekhai said to Rav Ashi:
This is what we say in the name of Reish Lakish:
Any 'common element' proof –
we refute it from within itself,
phrases.notes: He means you may only point to a strictness that ערלה and חמץ both share.

phrases.english: we do not refute it from the outside world.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב מָרְדֳּכַי לְרַב אָשֵׁי הָכִי אָמְרִינַן מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרֵישׁ לָקִישׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects רב אשי's answer in step 18, which brings the question of step 17 back.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: רב אשי's use of נבלה to refute the במה הצד
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: נבלה is an outside case, and a במה הצד can only be refuted from within its own sources.

steps.title: Then use a בְּמָה הַצַּד after all
steps.stepSummary: If נבלה cannot refute a בְּמָה הַצַּד, then ערלה and חמץ together should be enough to prove the law.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, let the law be learned through a בְּמָה הַצַּד.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to its earlier question. Since the נבלה refutation has just been rejected, why not learn the law from ערלה and חמץ together?
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב אשי's only objection to the בְּמָה הַצַּד was נבלה. רב מרדכי, quoting ריש לקיש, just removed that objection. So the question from step 17 comes back: why was כלאי הכרם needed at all?

keyTerms.meaning: If so: if what was just said is true
Learning a law from what two sources have in common
Let it come; let the law be learned this way

phrases.english: If so, let it be learned through a 'common element' proof?
phrases.notes: 'If so' means: if נבלה can't knock down a בְּמָה הַצַּד, as ריש לקיש just said.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the rejection of the נבלה refutation in step 19 and brings back the question of step 17.
steps.kashyaTarget: The use of כלאי הכרם as the source instead of a בְּמָה הַצַּד from ערלה and חמץ
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: With no valid refutation left, the simpler בְּמָה הַצַּד should work, so the extra source looks unnecessary.

steps.title: Both sources grow from the ground
steps.stepSummary: The בְּמָה הַצַּד fails because ערלה and חמץ share a feature that meat and milk lack: they both grow from the ground.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because it can be refuted: what is special about the common element of the two? They grow from the ground.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the בְּמָה הַצַּד does have a weakness that comes from inside its own sources. ערלה and חמץ both come from things that grow from the ground.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This refutation follows ריש לקיש's rule exactly: it points to something both sources share. Meat and milk do not grow from the ground, so maybe the benefit ban belongs only to plant products.

keyTerms.meaning: To refute; to knock down a proof
The shared feature of the sources
Things that grow from the ground

phrases.english: Because it can be refuted:
What about the common element between them?
phrases.notes: 'Them' means ערלה and חמץ.

phrases.english: They are things that grow from the ground.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 20.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Points to a weakness inside the sources themselves
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Without נבלה, the בְּמָה הַצַּד from ערלה and חמץ seemed solid.
steps.terutzMaskana: The shared 'grows from the ground' feature breaks the בְּמָה הַצַּד, so another source was needed.

steps.title: כלאי הכרם grows from the ground too
steps.stepSummary: The same refutation should also knock down the proof from כלאי הכרם, since it too grows from the ground.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, even now it can be refuted: what is special about כלאי הכרם? It grows from the ground.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns the last answer against the proof it is defending. כלאי הכרם also grows from the ground, so it should fail for the same reason.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If 'grows from the ground' is enough to break the ערלה and חמץ proof, it should also break a proof from כלאי הכרם. The source that was meant to fix the problem seems to have the very same weakness.

keyTerms.meaning: Even now; in the current version too
Mixed crops planted in a vineyard, which are forbidden for benefit

phrases.aramaic: אִי הָכִי, הַשְׁתָּא נָמֵי אִיכָּא לְמִיפְרַךְ:
phrases.english: If so, even now it can be refuted:

phrases.aramaic: מָה לְכִלְאֵי הַכֶּרֶם, שֶׁכֵּן גִּדּוּלֵי קַרְקַע?
phrases.english: What about כלאי הכרם? It grows from the ground!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי הָכִי, הַשְׁתָּא נָמֵי אִיכָּא לְמִיפְרַךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the answer of step 21 to attack the כלאי הכרם proof.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The same 'grows from the ground' refutation applies to כלאי הכרם, so it should fail just like the בְּמָה הַצַּד.

steps.title: Different rules for refuting different proofs
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש: a בְּמָה הַצַּד can be refuted by any shared feature, but a proof from a single source can only be refuted by a real stringency.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב מרדכי said to רב אשי: this is what we say in the name of ריש לקיש. Any בְּמָה הַצַּד can be refuted by anything at all. But a 'no, if you say' refutation of one case learned from one case only works through a קל וחומר. It cannot be done with just any difference.
steps.whatsHappening: רב מרדכי explains why 'grows from the ground' breaks the בְּמָה הַצַּד but not the proof from כלאי הכרם alone. The two kinds of proof follow different rules for being refuted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A בְּמָה הַצַּד rests only on what the sources share, so any shared feature the new case lacks can break it. A proof from one source can only be broken by pointing to a stringency that makes the source 'stricter'. 'Grows from the ground' is just a difference, not a stringency, so it does not break the כלאי הכרם proof.

keyTerms.meaning: Anything at all; any small difference
'No, if you say…': the standard way of refuting a proof
One case learned from one other case
Here: a refutation based on the source being stricter

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think the two refutations are equally strong. The same fact, 'grows from the ground', breaks a בְּמָה הַצַּד but is not enough against a proof from a single source.
steps.whyThisMatters: It sets a general rule for how strong a refutation must be, depending on the type of proof.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב מָרְדֳּכַי לְרַב אָשֵׁי:
phrases.english: רב מרדכי said to רב אשי:
This is what we say in the name of ריש לקיש:

phrases.aramaic: כֹּל מָה הַצַּד פָּרְכִינַן כֹּל דְּהוּ,
phrases.english: Any 'common element' proof, we refute with anything at all,
but a 'no, if you say' against one case learned from one case,
we refute only with a קל וחומר,
phrases.notes: He means only a point that makes the source stricter can knock down this kind of proof.

phrases.english: with just anything, we do not refute.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב מָרְדֳּכַי לְרַב אָשֵׁי: הָכִי אָמְרִינַן מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרֵישׁ לָקִישׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 22 by setting different rules for refuting each type of proof.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Draws a distinction in method between a בְּמָה הַצַּד and a single-source proof
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Any difference should refute any proof equally.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only a בְּמָה הַצַּד falls to any difference. A single-source proof needs a real stringency, so כלאי הכרם stands.

steps.title: Refute all three sources together
steps.stepSummary: כלאי הכרם is really added to ערלה and חמץ, so the proof is a בְּמָה הַצַּד of all three, and they all grow from the ground.
steps.simpleTranslation: Then let us refute all of them: what is special about all of them? They grow from the ground!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges again. כלאי הכרם is not standing alone; it is joined to ערלה and חמץ. So the proof is really a בְּמָה הַצַּד, and the 'anything at all' rule applies.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the proof uses all three sources together, it counts as a בְּמָה הַצַּד, not as one case learned from one case. Then any shared feature can break it, and all three grow from the ground. This brings back the problem that step 23 seemed to solve.

keyTerms.meaning: And let us refute
All of them together

phrases.english: But let us refute all of them:
phrases.notes: 'All of them' means ערלה, חמץ and כלאי הכרם taken together.

phrases.english: What about all of them? They all grow from the ground!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלִיפְרוֹךְ לְכוּלְּהוּ, מָה לְכוּלְּהוּ שֶׁכֵּן גִּדּוּלֵי קַרְקַע
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges step 23 by treating the כלאי הכרם proof as part of a three-source בְּמָה הַצַּד.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the כלאי הכרם proof counts as one case learned from one case
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Since כלאי הכרם is used together with ערלה and חמץ, the 'any difference' rule of בְּמָה הַצַּד applies, and all three share 'grows from the ground'.

steps.title: רב מרדכי introduces a different version of ריש לקיש's teaching
steps.stepSummary: After the challenge in step 24, רב מרדכי tells רב אשי that ריש לקיש's teaching was actually said differently, and he prepares to quote the new version.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רב מרדכי said to רב אשי: This is how we say it in the name of ריש לקיש:
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up its next move. It drops the version of ריש לקיש's teaching that was just challenged, and רב מרדכי gets ready to quote ריש לקיש a different way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 24 broke the earlier approach, because the proof turned out to rest on three sources that all grow from the ground. The word אֶלָּא tells us the גמרא accepts that challenge and does not try to defend the old version. Instead, it changes the report of what ריש לקיש actually said. The actual new teaching comes at the start of the next amud.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather. It shows the גמרא is dropping the approach it just had and switching to a new one.
This is how we say it. It introduces a different report of a teaching.
In the name of. It means passing on a teaching that came from an earlier sage.

steps.confusionAlert: Don't expect the answer in this line. It only introduces the new version, and the content of ריש לקיש's teaching comes right after.

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא, אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב מָרְדֳּכַי לְרַב אָשֵׁי,
phrases.english: Rather, Rav Mordekhai said to Rav Ashi:
This is how we say it in the name of Reish Lakish:

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא, אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב מָרְדֳּכַי לְרַב אָשֵׁי, הָכִי אָמְרִינַן מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרֵישׁ לָקִישׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Responds to step 24's challenge by dropping the version of ריש לקיש's teaching given in step 23 and introducing a different report of it.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Changes the report of what the earlier sage said (a different version of the teaching), instead of defending the old one.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: ריש לקיש's rule was that a single-source proof can only be refuted by a real stringency, which would save the כלאי הכרם proof.
steps.terutzMaskana: That version fails because the proof is really a בְּמָה הַצַּד. So ריש לקיש's teaching is reported a different way, and the new version follows.
